## Background Information

**NOTE: This file contains supporting matrix algebra and the fuller multiphase branch-flow formulation of Gan and Low [@gan2014convex]. The working equations are in `ch2_voltage_reactive_equations.qmd`.**

## Three-phase Branch Power Matrix

Recall that $\mathbf{\bar V}_i$ and $\mathbf{\bar I}_{ij}$ are $3\times1$ column vectors. We previously used the per-phase complex power vector:

$$\mathbf{\bar s}_{ij}=\begin{bmatrix}P_{ij}^a+jQ_{ij}^a\\P_{ij}^b+jQ_{ij}^b\\P_{ij}^c+jQ_{ij}^c\end{bmatrix}$$

Gan and Low also use the full branch power matrix:

$$\mathbf{\bar S}_{ij}=\mathbf{\bar V}_i\mathbf{\bar I}_{ij}^{H}$$ {#eq-background-branch-power-matrix}

Expanding the matrix multiplication:

$$
\mathbf{\bar S}_{ij}=
\begin{bmatrix}
\bar V_i^a(\bar I_{ij}^a)^* & \bar V_i^a(\bar I_{ij}^b)^* & \bar V_i^a(\bar I_{ij}^c)^*\\
\bar V_i^b(\bar I_{ij}^a)^* & \bar V_i^b(\bar I_{ij}^b)^* & \bar V_i^b(\bar I_{ij}^c)^*\\
\bar V_i^c(\bar I_{ij}^a)^* & \bar V_i^c(\bar I_{ij}^b)^* & \bar V_i^c(\bar I_{ij}^c)^*
\end{bmatrix}
$$

Note that the **diagonal elements** are the conventional complex powers for each phase:

$$\operatorname{diag}(\mathbf{\bar S}_{ij})=\mathbf{\bar s}_{ij}$$

The **off-diagonal elements** are cross-phase voltage-current products. They do not represent extra downstream branches or separate real/reactive phase powers. The full $3\times3$ matrix is useful for Gan and Low's branch-flow and optimization formulations, but it is not required just to substitute phase power into KVL.

## Derive the Magnitude of the Voltage

Following the same approach as in @eq-KVL3, we can obtain squared voltage magnitudes using the three-phase KVL equation:

$$\mathbf{\bar V}_j=\mathbf{\bar V}_i-\mathbf{\bar Z}_{ij}\mathbf{\bar I}_{ij}$$

To retain all cross-phase voltage products, multiply the equation on the right by its **Hermitian transpose**:

$$\mathbf{\bar V}_j\mathbf{\bar V}_j^H=(\mathbf{\bar V}_i-\mathbf{\bar Z}_{ij}\mathbf{\bar I}_{ij})(\mathbf{\bar V}_i-\mathbf{\bar Z}_{ij}\mathbf{\bar I}_{ij})^H$$ {#eq-kvl-complex-form-v-magnitude}

The Hermitian transpose, denoted by $H$, means **conjugate transpose**; it does **not** mean extracting the diagonal. A $3\times1$ voltage vector times its $1\times3$ conjugate transpose produces a $3\times3$ matrix.

### Solving for the left hand side of @eq-kvl-complex-form-v-magnitude

$$
\mathbf{\bar V}_j\mathbf{\bar V}_j^{H}
=\begin{bmatrix}\bar V_j^a\\\bar V_j^b\\\bar V_j^c\end{bmatrix}_{3\times1}
\begin{bmatrix}(\bar V_j^a)^*&(\bar V_j^b)^*&(\bar V_j^c)^*\end{bmatrix}_{1\times3}
=\begin{bmatrix}
|\bar V_j^a|^2&\bar V_j^a(\bar V_j^b)^*&\bar V_j^a(\bar V_j^c)^*\\
\bar V_j^b(\bar V_j^a)^*&|\bar V_j^b|^2&\bar V_j^b(\bar V_j^c)^*\\
\bar V_j^c(\bar V_j^a)^*&\bar V_j^c(\bar V_j^b)^*&|\bar V_j^c|^2
\end{bmatrix}_{3\times3}
$$ {#eq-voltage-matrix-magnitude}

Note that the diagonal elements are **squared** voltage magnitudes. The off-diagonal elements remain complex cross-phase voltage products.

Gan and Low define the voltage matrix as:

$$\mathbf{\bar W}_j=\mathbf{\bar V}_j\mathbf{\bar V}_j^H$$ {#eq-voltage-wj}

Similarly:

$$\mathbf{\bar W}_i=\mathbf{\bar V}_i\mathbf{\bar V}_i^H$$ {#eq-voltage-wi}

### Solving for the right hand side of @eq-kvl-complex-form-v-magnitude

We can apply the same Hermitian transpose to the right-hand side:

$$\mathbf{\bar W}_j=(\mathbf{\bar V}_i-\mathbf{\bar Z}_{ij}\mathbf{\bar I}_{ij})(\mathbf{\bar V}_i^H-\mathbf{\bar I}_{ij}^H\mathbf{\bar Z}_{ij}^H)$$

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
## Voltage Eq. Note

$$(\mathbf{\bar Z}\mathbf{\bar I})^H=\mathbf{\bar I}^H\mathbf{\bar Z}^H$$

The multiplication order reverses because $(AB)^H=B^HA^H$. This is a property of the conjugate transpose, not merely a rule for fixing dimensions.
:::

Expanding the right-hand side:

$$\mathbf{\bar W}_j=\mathbf{\bar V}_i\mathbf{\bar V}_i^H-\mathbf{\bar V}_i\mathbf{\bar I}_{ij}^H\mathbf{\bar Z}_{ij}^H-\mathbf{\bar Z}_{ij}\mathbf{\bar I}_{ij}\mathbf{\bar V}_i^H+\mathbf{\bar Z}_{ij}\mathbf{\bar I}_{ij}\mathbf{\bar I}_{ij}^H\mathbf{\bar Z}_{ij}^H$$ {#eq-voltage-three-phase-kvl-matrix}

We previously defined the voltage matrix in @eq-voltage-wi and the branch-power matrix in @eq-background-branch-power-matrix. Accordingly, we can define the current outer-product matrix as:

$$\mathbf{\bar L}_{ij}=\mathbf{\bar I}_{ij}\mathbf{\bar I}_{ij}^H$$

Therefore, @eq-voltage-three-phase-kvl-matrix can be written as:

$$\boxed{\mathbf{\bar W}_j=\mathbf{\bar W}_i-\mathbf{\bar S}_{ij}\mathbf{\bar Z}_{ij}^H-\mathbf{\bar Z}_{ij}\mathbf{\bar S}_{ij}^H+\mathbf{\bar Z}_{ij}\mathbf{\bar L}_{ij}\mathbf{\bar Z}_{ij}^H}$$ {#eq-background-voltage-matrix}

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
## Note

@eq-background-voltage-matrix is an exact squared-voltage **matrix** relationship derived from KVL. The term $\mathbf{\bar Z}_{ij}\mathbf{\bar L}_{ij}\mathbf{\bar Z}_{ij}^H$ is quadratic in line current; it is the outer product of the line voltage-drop vector with itself. Its diagonal is not the same as the real-power loss. For our immediate voltage–reactive-power work, the per-phase power equations and KVL are sufficient as starting equations, so we can keep this fuller derivation for background.
:::
